ABSENCE_CLAIM_RE now requires a path/file/directory noun next to the ambiguous words (exists/absent/removed/deleted/gone), or one of a fixed set of unambiguous phrases (no longer exists/no longer present/not present/does not exist); a differently-worded content-vs-path distinction outside both of those shapes — e.g. an absence claim that names neither a path noun nor one of the listed phrases — would still fall through to the existence-only rejection, and a content-removal claim that happens to mention the word 'file' in passing (e.g. 'the token was removed from the file's header comment') could still wrongly pass; this was scoped to the exact ambiguity Greptile's finding demonstrated, not an exhaustive claim-intent parser

Superseded twice: first by the sibling-path-exactness/ordering round (restricting the exception to test -f/-e via FILE_EXISTENCE_PROBE_RE, exact path-token equality, sibling strictly earlier than the compound), then by this round, which extends FILE_EXISTENCE_PROBE_RE to -f/-e/-d/-r and normalizes path tokens (./X vs X) before comparing. As of this round: a test -d or test -r sibling now corroborates the same as -f/-e, and an equivalent relative spelling of the same path now matches. What is still NOT covered, and remains fail-closed as padding: any other flag (test -n/-z, ...), a substring/near-match path even after normalization, a non-test-shaped existence probe like `find . -name X`, a path made equivalent only by resolving `..` against a working directory the gate does not know (normpath collapses `./` and doubled separators lexically, it does not consult the filesystem), and a same-path match recorded AFTER the compound. Still intentionally conservative/fail-closed, not an exhaustive parser of every way existence could be proven.

The ordering requirement added this round (sibling command index < quiet-search command index) is enforced on the receipt's own array order, not on wall-clock timestamps — no per-command timestamp is recorded anywhere in this schema, so a receipt author who lists commands out of true execution order could still satisfy the check by construction. This trusts array order as a proxy for execution order, the same trust this gate already places in 'commands' elsewhere (e.g. nothing stops a receipt from listing any command in a fabricated sequence); closing that would need per-command timestamps in the schema, which is out of scope for this round's fix.

Superseded twice more by later rounds (see new commands/claims below for the latest): the round-8 fix first stopped _normalize_path() from collapsing ANY trailing slash — right for -f/-e/-r, where the slash can flip the answer, but it also (wrongly) made 'test -d config' and 'test -d config/' compare unequal, since a directory check's own predicate already requires the target to resolve as a directory and the slash can never change ITS answer (Greptile P1, 'Directory probes treated as different'). This round's fix makes the collapse flag-aware via _TRAILING_SLASH_SAFE_FLAGS = {'d'}: only -d collapses the slash; -f/-e/-r keep it significant, exactly as round 8 intended for them. _normalize_path() still does not touch case, does not resolve symlinks, and does not consult the filesystem at all, so two paths that are the same file only via a symlink, a case-insensitive filesystem, or a mount bind are still compared as different tokens and would not corroborate each other — that remains out of scope, a real limitation but not a correctness bug the way the trailing-slash cases were.

Superseded by this round's fix (see new commands/claims below): the round-8 sibling-flag check required byte-for-byte flag equality between a sibling and the compound's own gate, which was itself flagged as a bug (Greptile P1, 'Valid probes rejected') because it rejected the sound case where a stricter sibling (-f, -d, -r) corroborates a weaker -e gate on the same path — passing -f proves -e would pass too, since being a regular file requires existing. This round replaces exact equality with the one-way _FLAG_IMPLIES lattice (documented above) that accepts that sound direction while still rejecting the unsound one (-e sibling corroborating an -f gate) and cross-type mismatches (-d vs -f). The lattice only models existence-implication, not any deeper semantic relationship (e.g. it does not know that a file's -r and -f might both be independently provable some other way); a receipt relying on any predicate relationship this lattice doesn't encode is still correctly rejected as a flag mismatch. This was scoped to the exact soundness gap Greptile demonstrated, not to building an exhaustive semantic model of every POSIX test flag relationship.

_FLAG_IMPLIES (this round) is a hand-written lattice over exactly the four flags FILE_EXISTENCE_PROBE_RE recognises (f/e/d/r); it is not derived from, or checked against, any formal model of POSIX test(1) semantics, so a fifth flag added to that regex in the future would need its implications added to the lattice by hand too — nothing enforces that the two stay in sync beyond code review.
